newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast crudes ease on WTI, thin buying.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast crudes ease on WTI, thin buying.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crude prices shaved five cents from Thursday's levels, tracking West Texas Intermediate (WTI), while Alaskan crude trade continued to languish with no buying interest.
With refining margins poor and supply ample, refiners continued to hold off buying Alaska North Slope crude at the going offer of $2.10 minus December WTI, traders said.
Major buyers kept their bids at $2.50 under.
Buyers claimed a major producer sold spot barrels of ANS crude to Far East markets to make up for the slump in trade.
Meanwhile, West Coast buyers received needed oil on a formula-trade basis.
Formula trade is a method of buying ANS off a long-term average rather than a spot discount to WTI.
The diff for ANS stayed unchanged at $2.30 a barrel under December WTI.
Wilmington crude fell 50 cents with a drop posted prices. Traders talked premiums at plus 50 to 60 cents over postings, putting outright prices at $18.40/18.50 a barrel.
Kern River heavy crude also fell as major oil companies lowered postings.

Postings fell 60 cents, with dealers discussing differentials of minus 10 and plus 10 cents a barrel. Outright prices were down to $16.80/17.00 a barrel. --David Brinkerhoff, Los Angeles energy +1 213 380 2014
